sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in L.P.No.37/2019 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against him are under Sections 406 and 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. It is stated that the case against him happened to be transferred to the Long Pending Register,
since the petitioner was abroad in connection with his employment.
Now the petitioner wants to surrender before the learned Magistrate, and to abide by the due process of law, in connection with the crime alleged against him.

3. The present petition is filed for a direction to the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Tripunithura, to consider the bail application of the petitioner on the day when he appeares before the Trial Court, and to keep the Non-Bailable Warrant ordered against him in abeyance, so that he will be able to surrender before the said court.

entities.text:
Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Tripunithura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner apprehends remand to judicial custody on the date of 2025:KER:49473 his surrender before the learned Magistrate, and it is due to that reason that he has approached this Court with this petition.
5. It appears that the failure of the petitioner to appear before the learned Magistrate was due to his employment abroad.

Since the Final Report in the crime alleged against the petitioner is already filed, and the matter is pending consideration before the learned Magistrate, the custody of the petitioner is not at all required for any purpose related to the investigation.

That apart, if the contention of the petitioner about his employment abroad as the reason for not appearing before the learned Magistrate is correct, it cannot be said to be wilful disobedience to the process of court.
All these aspects have to be considered by the learned Magistrate, while deciding the bail application filed by the petitioner.

6. Every court in our country are bound to follow the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2018 (1) KHC 901], about the humanitarian approach to be taken by Courts dealing with bail matters.

entities.text: Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2018 (1) KHC 901]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I deem it appropriate to dispose of this Crl.M.C., directing the learned Magistrate to consider the bail application, if any, filed by the petitioner, preferably on the Biju Nair vs State Of Kerala on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128550299/
2 same day of his surrender, and to decide the matter in accordance with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid decision (supra), as well as all other judicial precedents on this point.
